summary: Smith Knob, in Idaho County on the Payette National Forest, went from a 1929 log cabin to a 1958 concrete base with a flat cab, and was demolished in 2008.

facts.design: Log cabin (1929), then a 10-foot concrete base with a flat cab (1958); the 2008 report calls the demolished structure a two-story ground cabin

events.note: The first structure on the site was a log cabin.
A 10-foot concrete base with a flat cab was built.
Anna M Weskema is listed for 1969-1971.
Last used in the 1970s; the exact year is not given.
Demolished in 2008; the 2008 Western Region report says the Payette National Forest removed two unused lookouts that year.

corrections.why: FireLookout.com places the lookout in Idaho County, Idaho; the brief's county field repeats the state name.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not reconciled. FireLookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts describe a 1929 log cabin then a 1958 concrete base with a flat cab, while the 2008 report calls the demolished structure a two-story ground cabin. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Demolition in 2008 is supported by all three sources. No source describes what remains on the site today. The Drive-Up and Demolished tags describe the lookout as it was, so the story does not treat them as a current access statement, and no visit facts or access level are recorded. The brief's design field '2-story ground cabin' comes from the 2008 report and conflicts with the other two sources.
